AudioTune - running it on another computer
==========================================

WINDOWS (64-bit)

Copy audiotune.exe anywhere and double-click it. That is the whole install.

The executable is self-contained: it links only against DLLs that ship with
Windows (kernel32, user32, gdi32, ole32, opengl32, and so on). There is no
runtime to install, no Visual C++ redistributable, no Rust, no MinGW.

Requirements on the target machine:
  - 64-bit Windows 10 or 11
  - Working audio drivers (WASAPI, which is every normal Windows machine)
  - OpenGL 3.3, which any graphics driver from the last decade provides

Before opening the audio streams, allow microphone access:
  Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone > let desktop apps access

And turn off every microphone effect, or the measurements are worthless:
  Sound settings > (your mic) > Properties > Advanced / Enhancements
  Disable noise suppression, echo cancellation, AGC and "microphone boost".

If the window does not appear, run it from a command prompt to see why:

    audiotune.exe --list-devices     lists every audio device it can see
    audiotune.exe --selftest         opens the real streams and records 1.5 s
                                     of room noise (it plays nothing)

If it reports an OpenGL problem, the machine has no usable graphics driver.
Install the vendor driver, or drop a software-rendering opengl32.dll (Mesa
llvmpipe for Windows) next to the exe.

Over Remote Desktop, OpenGL is often unavailable. Use the machine directly, or
use the two command-line modes above.


LINUX (64-bit)

There is no prebuilt binary here; build it on the target machine:

    sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libasound2-dev \
                     libgl1-mesa-dev libxkbcommon-dev
    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
    cargo build --release

The binary lands in target/release/audiotune. cpal uses ALSA, and picks up JACK
automatically if it is running. File dialogs go through the XDG desktop portal,
which every normal desktop has.

Add yourself to the audio group for lower-latency access:

    sudo usermod -aG audio $USER      (log out and back in)


MOVING YOUR WORK BETWEEN MACHINES

Everything is in the project file saved from the top bar: measurements, impulse
responses, target curve, filters, microphone calibration and the EQ unit
description. Copy the .atune file across and open it on the other machine.
